settings.title: Enable two-factor authentication
settings.description: Add a second factor (authenticator app or SMS) to your Twitch account login. 2FA is disabled by default for viewers; streamers are required to enable it before broadcasting or receiving payouts. Twitch supports TOTP authenticator apps on desktop and SMS-only on mobile. FIDO2/U2F security keys are not supported. Your email must be verified before the 2FA option appears.

settings.title: Disable personalized advertising
settings.description: Opt out of interest-based advertising by disabling the 'Show me personalised ads' toggle. By default, Twitch and its ad vendors use analytics and tracking cookies to tailor advertisements to your perceived interests. Disabling this toggle turns off ad personalization across all listed ad vendors simultaneously. EU users can additionally manage preferences via the 'Ad' icon on advertisements.

settings.title: Review and revoke unused third-party app connections
settings.description: Periodically audit all third-party applications (e.g., Streamlabs, OBS, Stream Deck, Discord, YouTube, Steam) that have OAuth access to your Twitch account. Revoke tokens for any apps you no longer use. The 'Other Connections' section lists every app you have authorized. Twitch recommends auditing connections at least twice a year to reduce the attack surface for account takeover.

settings.title: Block whispers from strangers
settings.description: Enable the 'Block Whispers from Strangers' toggle to restrict private messages (whispers) to only friends, followed accounts, subscribers, moderators, and editors. When enabled, strangers receive a silent fail and cannot reach you. The whisper inbox is a known vector for phishing links, scam follow-up DMs, and unsolicited harassment. Note: if you initiate a whisper to a stranger, they can temporarily reply for 48 hours. Twitch requires a verified phone number to send whispers.

settings.title: Disable sharing viewing activity
settings.description: Turn off the 'Share My Activity' toggle to prevent your viewing and broadcasting activity from being visible to your friends list. This setting is enabled by default, exposing which streams you are watching to anyone on your friends list. Disabling it improves privacy by hiding your real-time viewing behavior from other users.

settings.title: Disconnect all other sessions periodically
settings.description: Use the 'Disconnect all other sessions' button to terminate any active login sessions on other devices or browsers. This is especially important after a password change, suspected account compromise, or when using shared/public computers. Twitch does not automatically expire old sessions, so manual review is recommended.

settings.title: Opt out of cross-context behavioral advertising
settings.description: Opt out of the sharing of personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising as defined by the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA) and similar state laws. This can be done via the Global Privacy Control (GPC) browser signal or through the Twitch Privacy Choices page. This is separate from the in-product ad personalization toggle and covers data shared with third parties beyond Twitch's ad vendors.
